body.p: There lived a man, a master of nomadizing and hunting. His wife was living with their little son in their small yurt. When they were in the yurt, something rustled, they looked: Chulugdi is coming. She entered their small yurt, she swallowed the woman immediately, she didn't swallow the son. Having eaten [the woman], Chulugdi started to live in the small yurt of the man. The man came home in the evening, he entered the small yurt. Chulugdi is living in his yurt, she has eaten his wife, [but] his son is alive, she didn't eat [him]. The man was afraid. "She'll eat me", the man said. He married Chulugdi for that she doesn't eat him. At night he sleeps with Chulugdi. The man got up early in the many, he caught his reindeer, he said to his wife Chulugdi: "Having loaded [the reindeer], follow my ski track". [DCh]: Verb form "ÉmÉhindÉËwi" is not clear. No imperative marker there like in the translation. Having said [this] the man put on his skis, he went to his elder brother. He came to his elder brother, he came there and began to tell his elder brother: "Chulugdi came and ate my wandering guide [=wife]". The relatives of the man got afraid, then the man said: "Brother, let's light a fire! Let me push her into the bonfire." There they lit a bonfire. The woman Chulugdi loaded the reindeer, she sat the child on a riding reindeer [with its face] behind. When she was about to leave the child fell onto the ground. Chulugdi came to the child, she sat it [with the face] back onto the riding reindeer saying to the child: "I'll swallow you, if you fall down. How did your mother seat you?" "Mother turned my face to the reindeer's antlers". Chulugdi seated the child like that. Now they wandered along the man's ski track. They wandered and wandered, then they came to the camp. The man's younger sisters met them and said: "Sister-in-law, let us unload [the reindeer]". The girls unloaded [the reindeer]. When sitting at the fire, the men laughed and said: "The hook [for hanging up the kettle] fell down, who can get it out?" There the man said: "My wife will get it out". He said to his wife Chulugdi: "Old woman, go and get [it]". That one jumped up, came and wanted to take it. There they pushed her into the bonfire. Chulugdi's eye bursted in the fire and burned. So they killed Chulugdi. The people say: "If Chulugdi's eye doesn't burn, if it doesn't burst, Chulugdi won't die. Her whole body is iron, only one eye is human-like".
